questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic opportunities were important to me. I knew from friends and research that St Andrews University had an excellent school of IR. Which I highly valued. I had learned that the teachers were very personal with their students and classes very small and intimate to improve the participation of every individual in the class. I was also very intrigued by the scenery. It is a beautiful old town with long beaches on one side and green fields on the other side of the town. Furthermore, I prioritised an English speaking destination to improve my English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I loved the destination and the experience. I made some great friends and was lucky to get close with many permanent students. The only downsides of my exchange were mainly due to covid.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find information upon arrival, but I think this is mainly because of Covid. Because of covid, the help desk was closed - and there honestly wasn't much help to get from the school. Luckily my roommates were very friendly and helpful. The school didn't share information on the condition of our schooling before the term started, and our schedule was not ready before classes began either.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, there wasn't any assistance upon arrival. But throughout the semester, the global office was very present and helpful. They even hosted events and socials for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy! I found a Facebook group called "get a room at St Andrew". Through this, I talked to many different people, and I found my lovely roommates and a house with them quite close to the city. Residence in St Andrews is quite expensive. Therefore, I was pleased to find a place around the same cost as a room in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In my experience, it was the perfect solution because many of the older permanent students live off-campus. Being an exchange student, you are often not a first-year student, and therefore you might have more luck finding people somewhat your age to live with off-campus. They introduced me to all the socials and their friend groups. Furthermore, it is much cheaper than living on campus. Even an expensive off-campus residence downtown is more affordable than a campus residence. A downside is that many exchange students don't know this, so they live on-campus homes. I didn't mean that many exchange students before white late in my stay, but instead, I found some good friends around the permanent students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Use facebook groups to get advice and find housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered through an online portal and was in contact with the global office during the process. Overall it was straightforward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Upon registration, the global office was very helpful and quickly replied to my questions and worries.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes, I was. The registration of classes happened very late. Almost only a couple of weeks before class started. Because I needed to be enrolled in the specific courses, KU asked for, the lateness of the process was a worrying factor. I was told that one of the classes was full but that I had to wait till late August to talk to my course coordinator. Obviously, this was a bit worrying, but as soon as late August came and I could talk to my coordinator, he was incredibly helpful and ensured that everything got sorted out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration is closed over the summer, so there is no need to stress unnecessarily at that time, but make sure to contact them as soon as it opens in August, and they will be helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am pleased with my exchange. That being said, I enjoy actual physical classes, workshops, discussions and more. The lessons I took at St Andrews didn't include much of this. On the other hand, the small size of the classes did ensure the quality of the physical lessons we had.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels I took was supposed to be relatively high. Courses you take on your last year of the bachelor. But I don't think the level felt necessarily more elevated than the courses I've taken at Copenhagen University. There was, of course, a language barrier at first, but I fast overcame that.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is very different from KU. There was a lot less teaching in the classes I took and a lot more time to study yourself, but the teachers offer lots of personal office hours. Ultimately, students do have the chance to get more face to face teaching from the professors. Versus KU, which schedules a lot of in-class time with professors and older students to help one understand the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
IR3056 Political Leadership: Theories and History
IR3039 International Relations of the European Union

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: IR3039 International Relations of the European Union

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: School events turned out to be rather expensive. And sports clubs was an unexpected cost as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I got lucky with housing which could otherwise have been 8000 dkk per month. School events though where very expensive. Between 1000 and 2000 dkk per month, as every big school event was between 400 and 800 dkk and smaller events was 80 and 150 dkk.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Very many sports clubs were available and lots of social and creative clubs as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join as many sports clubs as possible. They give you a chance to try new sports which is so much fun and get new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Islands and highlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. The Scottish culture (and British as lot's of British people study at St Andrews) is quite easy to get on with. The humour is sort of familiar to the Danish humour.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the different clubs, and don't be afraid to talk to people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think it was rather the culture of the school than the actual culture that was a big change from what I'm used to. It is a culture where you either socialize or study. There is no time for a chill. But that was a part of the experience and really fun.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most of it. The humour is great, the society and social life at St Andrews, the competitive culture that makes every student aim for the highest.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If the student is going on exchange from Danish university they are usually older than student living in student housing, take your time to find a good housing situation with older students. Be aware that the semester is very short. I would recommend maybe doing two semesters. It is an expensive destination.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the facebook groups: fx find a room st andrews and contact the global office.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding my roommates and friends. And visiting the highlands and islands. The nature in Scotland is unbelievable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think there were any great exchange related challenges. Being one of the only danish exchanges and living among permanent students, I did have to put myself out there a lot. But it was for the best and I got some great friends and the true St Andrews experience from it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
